measurement_policy: Original thresholds and automated screens retained. Manual observations are separate; no decks, rules or pilot changes.

evidence: Mortify removed GGS at own turn3; reentered turn6 and first Dragon turn9. Fumigate and Fell the Mighty later interrupted development.
At global turn51 / own turn13, two GGS Dragon tokens (IDs496,535) each dealt5 combat damage to Gabe_Food, whose life fell5 to-5.
GGS attacked in the same combat, received4 damage from three blockers, went to graveyard/command, and was recast in main2 using ten logged mana-source activations.
Every recorded own COMBAT_BEGIN from turns13 through18 had GGS present and fresh_ready=0. No later GGS Dragon creation was observed.
reviews.interpretation: The fixed15/20 pressure threshold missed an actual opponent elimination. This game is not evidence of insufficient natural Dragon payoff. Early disruption/recovery was costly, but terminal lack of fresh attack-ready creatures is a separate ammunition observation. The commander attack/recast is a pilot-risk example; its tactical necessity is not proven.
reviews.limits: No replayed alternative line; no causal claim that another card or withholding GGS would win the game.

reviews.review_kind: War Cadence plausibility, competing mana, and copy logging
evidence: Student ID350 copied Prosperous Thief on own turn5 and returned via Reanimate as Eagles of the North on turn7. The summary previously retained only its first copy; repeated-entry logging was corrected uniformly.
The resolution description says Reanimate loses0 life, but the adjacent canonical Life event says40 to36; actual observed loss4. No missing-life-loss gameplay error is established.

Fresh Lagomos Elementals were blocked on own turns7,8,9,10 while GGS was operational in those combats. Turns7 and8 had screened combat-begin untapped budget0; actual spells included commander redeployment (both turns) and Reanimate (turn7).

Turn10 had own screened budget8 and a Cadence activation screen4, assuming Cadence was already deployed. Same-turn actions were Shadow Rift on GGS, Professional Face-Breaker, and Swiftfoot Boots on the Student/Eagles copy.
reviews.interpretation: An observed access stall and a plausible already-deployed Cadence window exist. Recasts consume mana on earlier blocked turns; cheaper access is in hand but the observed turn10 Shadow Rift target is GGS rather than the fresh Elemental. Presence of access cards is not proof of successful access deployment. The already-deployed screen omits Cadence's casting cost and cannot establish a changed outcome.
reviews.limits: No replayed counterfactual, exact payment attribution, or isolated Student-versus-Cadence causal effect. Do not conclude that the replacement was correct from copy choices alone.

reviews.review_kind: Healthy commander / Dragon attrition; payoff falsification candidate
evidence: GGS remained operational with no logged commander disruption. Actual Dragon production on own turns5,6,7,8 was1,2,1,1 respectively, with recurring Fire Navy Trebuchet ammunition.
Gabe exiled Dragon425 with Anguished Unmaking at global turn21. Jaymie exiled Dragon446 through Etrata at turn28. Gabe destroyed Dragon435 with Mortify at turn29.
Surviving Dragons dealt10 combat damage at own turn7 and5 at turn8. The five produced Dragons did not survive together as a lethal army.
reviews.interpretation: The engine created five Dragons with uninterrupted GGS and recurring ammunition, yet never crossed the pressure threshold before losing. Targeted exile/removal suppressed the actual Dragon board. This is the strongest reviewed challenge to delayed natural combat payoff so far: broader protection, higher production throughput, or earlier payoff delivery could matter. It does not prove a healthy surviving Dragon army lacks power, nor does it prove that protection alone or an extra payoff card would solve the state.
reviews.limits: No causal alternate-line replay. Broad protection/recovery here includes preserving the produced Dragon board, not commander disruption alone.

reviews.review_kind: Control wins without GGS ignition; threshold limitation
evidence: GGS was first cast on own turn11; no GGS-created Dragon was observed. The control won on own turn12.
Fallen Shinobi was reanimated on turn3, Purphoros cast turn5, and Goldspan repeatedly cast on turns6,7,8,9; Goldspan generated observed Treasure on turns6 through11.
Pre-ignition total damage reached16 on own turn7, and lower distributed damage continued.
reviews.interpretation: The control has an observed fallback win without natural GGS production. A threat proxy restricted to post-ignition states misses this win; report fallback victories separately. This is evidence of independent package contribution, not proof that the five-part GGS architecture cannot win or that each removed payoff card is necessary.
reviews.limits: One illustrative game, not isolated card causality. No recommendation to restore a generic fireworks package solely from this result.

reviews.review_kind: Independent payoff candidate; blocker and opponent-race review
evidence: GGS cast own turn4; three Dragons created on own turns5,6,8; no observed commander disruption or wipe. Goldspan returned Treasure; hand count remained five at beginning of own turns6 and8.
GGS Dragons dealt5 combat damage on turns6,7,8. At turn7 Shadow Rift targeted an existing Dragon while the fresh Goldspan was blocked; no fresh connection that combat.

Own turn8 combat sent the board at Destyn and dealt12 combat damage including5 from a GGS Dragon; Destyn ultimately lost from life reaching zero. The fixed15/20 whole-board pressure threshold was not crossed.
On the next observed opposing combat, Combustion Man dealt15 damage from its attack trigger (Pure life24 to9); fresh Dragon459 blocked it but ten combat damage from other attackers reduced Pure to-1.
reviews.interpretation: An uninterrupted commander and repeated Dragon production did not beat the surviving opponent in time, but natural Dragon damage contributed to eliminating Destyn. Access allocation and defensive choices coexist with slow payoff delivery and an opponent burst. This is not a clean proof that a functioning surviving Dragon army lacks lethal power, nor should it be dismissed automatically as commander protection failure.
reviews.limits: No alternate-line replay; exact causality of access, target selection, defense and earlier payoff is unresolved.
